issues.area: test gap (R-SYN-13 [MUST] 'without polling'; F-30's 'at most once per edge')
issues.problem:
In mutant M-EDGESTART that line is deleted, so every attempt records edge serial 0. The whole ZTronAssetSyncTests suite still passes under it: 257 of 257, exit 0.

My scratch probe PROBE-C10R-1 builds the case: a prefetch member is running, the path goes offline, then back to unrestricted (one satisfied edge), and every later attempt is scripted to fail with .offline(.noConnection).
- At HEAD, in 3 of 3 runs: 'starts 2 state failed(whenOnline)'. The member is retried at once a single time, then waits for the next edge.
- Under M-EDGESTART, in 3 of 3 runs: 'starts 21 state downloading'. It is still restarting when the probe stops at epoch + 20.

So the bound that keeps R-SYN-13 free of polling, which F-30 states, is pinned by no test. Without it, any path whose connections keep failing offline while it reads satisfied would restart in a hot loop with no backoff.
issues.fix: Commit PROBE-C10R-1 as an R-SYN-13 regression test. After one edge, a member whose attempts keep failing offline while the path reads satisfied starts exactly twice and then waits in failed(whenOnline). Show that it fails under M-EDGESTART.

issues.location: Sources/ZTronAssetSync/Engine/EngineJobs.swift:119-137 (addInterest: wasReleasedOnly leads to enqueue(transfer, front: true)); joinMember in EngineCommands.swift:258-277
issues.problem:
Every queued job that only released groups want, set aside or still in place, is pushed to the front of its lane when an interest joins it.

PROBE-C10R-3 (scratch): a handle of releasesPerTurn + 64 members is released, then three of its still-pending members gain an interest one after the other in the same turn. They were joined in the order a409ae, 5c88c8, 2c725b, and the queue head became 2c725b, 5c88c8, a409ae: reversed. They also move ahead of prefetch work that was queued earlier.

A new handle overlapping a large released one hits this path through joinMember. Its re-joined members then dispatch in reverse id order. Before cycle 10 those entries kept their place in the queue.

The doc comment's 'at the front of its lane, where it waited' is inaccurate. No requirement fixes the order within a lane.

issues.area: test flake (L4-R8): failed in the required iOS Simulator run
issues.location: Tests/ZTronAssetSyncTests/Engine/EngineRegressionCycle9Tests.swift:42-54 (the 10,000-yield wait for the sleeper's registration) and :59
issues.problem:
The official iOS Simulator run failed one test.
- Device: 5B940E6E, iOS 27.0, 1-minute load 44 to 68.
- xcresult: 1050 passed, 1 failed.
- The failing test is EngineRegressionCycle9Tests/drivingStopsBeforeReturning(): 'Expectation failed: unseen == 0 / unseen → 1: the sleeper never registered in 1 rounds'.

The test waits at most 10,000 Task.yield()s for an unstructured Task to call clock.sleep. How many yields that takes depends on scheduling.

PROBE-C10C-7 ran the same rounds as 16 parallel instances of 2,000 rounds each, at load 85 to 91. The most yields needed before registration ranged from 2 to 921 per instance, a heavy tail. Under the simulator's in-process contention it once exceeded 10,000, and the test fails.

A second simulator run of ZTronAssetSyncTests passed (257 of 257), so the failure is intermittent: a flake.
issues.fix:
Make the wait deterministic:
- Replace the capped yield loop with `await clock.waitForSleepers(atLeast: 1)` (ManualTimeSource API). A stale driver can advance the clock only to a registered sleeper's deadline, so this returns in both outcomes.
- Or remove the 10,000 cap and loop until the sleeper registers or the clock moves, bounded by the test's 1-minute time limit.
- Keep the stale and unseen assertions.

Show that the test still fails against the cycle-8 driver as a mutant. Record the change in F-17 under L4-R8.

issues.area: test flake (L4-R8; L4-V3-00 only partly fixed): the lower bound still depends on scheduling
issues.problem:
The test failed in my stress run: `swift test --filter 'EngineRegressionCycle9Tests|EngineEventsTests' --repeat-until fail --maximum-repetitions 15`. It stopped after about 14 iterations (1-minute load 21 falling to 12, 5-minute load 58 falling to 48) with 'R-SYN-12: transfer progress published to subscribers never exceeds 10 Hz per asset under ManualTimeSource … Expectation failed: progress.count >= 2'.

Cause, as a timeline: each round waits for liveCount == 0, releases a progress update, advances the clock 0.02 s, then waits for running == 1. Nothing waits for the engine's driver to apply the released update before the clock moves. So updates are applied, and rate-limited, at whatever later clock instant the driver happens to reach.

PROBE-C10C-6 runs the same loop and reads active.bytesReceived after each round. Across 20 parallel iterations:
- in 34 to 50 of the 50 rounds, the clock advanced before the engine had applied that round's update;
- the progress-event count varied from 3 to 11.

When the driver is starved, nearly all updates are applied at one late instant, and the count falls below 2. Run alone, the test passed 400 times, and the events suite passed 40 times at load 5 to 9, so the failure is intermittent.
issues.fix:
In each round, after `harness.source.release(...)`, wait until the engine has applied that round's update, before `harness.time.advance(by: 0.02)`:
`await engine.awaitCondition { $0.state.jobs[entry.transferID]?.active?.bytesReceived == Int64(10 + round) }`

Each update is then published, or rate-limited, at its own round's instant. The count becomes deterministic, and the lower bound can assert the exact expected count. Record the change in F-17 under L4-R8.

issues.area: residue / by design (not a regression): the first conditions element after the watcher starts is never an edge
issues.location: Sources/ZTronAssetSync/Engine/EngineConditions.swift:91 (`previous.map {...} ?? false`); EngineDispatch.swift gate (a user lane may start with conditions == nil); EngineFailures.swift:84
issues.problem:
The gate lets a user-initiated attempt start before the watcher's first element, while conditions == nil. If the first element applied is satisfied, networkEdgeSerial does not move. An .offline failure after it is then failed(whenOnline), and the waiter is answered .offline.

My first PROBE-C10C-2a variant sent the element before the watcher read its initial one, and got 'failure(.offline) starts 1'. This matches F-16/L4-R3: a path that reads satisfied while connections fail waits for an edge. It is not a liveness defect for a waiter. I did not build a probe for a group member at user-initiated priority in this window.
issues.fix:
Optional:
- At attempt start, when conditions == nil, record a sentinel edge serial, so the first satisfied element counts as an edge for that attempt.
- Otherwise, note the case in F-16/F-30.

issues.problem:
Every interest addition goes through addInterest. Only continueReleases empties `releasing`, and it restores the set-aside entries when it does. A job only released groups want can lose interests but never gain a non-released one except through addInterest. scan's single rebuild is correct for the take and peek cases.

In a scratch copy I added the invariant that every queued job has a valid live-queue entry, or is only wanted by released groups and has its entry aside. It held:
- across the whole Sync suite and my probes;
- in a randomized model with releasesPerTurn = 1, 40 entries, groups of up to 24 at random lanes, 8 seeds of 10,000 operations: 0 violations, with set-aside reached 0 to 6 times per seed.

PROBE-C10C-4b: re-registering the last 40 members of a released 2,000-member handle keeps all 40 jobs; they start and none is stranded.

The engine's own invariant check has no 'queued job reachable' rule, so a future stranding would go unnoticed.
issues.fix: Optional: add the reachability rule to invariantViolations. It is test-only and costs one pass over the queues.

fix10.summary:
Close-out cycle 10 for WP-F on wp/f (worktree /Users/admin/Documents/ZTronAssetKit/.worktrees/f). All three blocking findings were reproduced at b9acb51, and each had its failing test committed before its fix.

**Blocking fixes**
1. **Releasing a user-initiated prefetch handle held the actor 22 ms (C2, PROBE-C9C-2).**
   - At b9acb51 the new release benchmark measured 22.13, 22.16 and 22.00 ms.
   - Fix (dca73b9, simplified in 51ef016): a scan now takes the queue entry of a job that only released groups want out of its queue, so each entry is stepped over once. The aside list lives in LaneQueues (pop/peek take a setAside predicate).
   - The pump's pop and hasQueuedUser() set such entries aside. addInterest queues the job again when an interest joins it at its own lane. continueReleases restores any valid aside entry once no release is left. The invariant check flags an aside entry whose job another interest wants.
   - After: 4.12, 4.18 and 4.21 ms. The prefetch-lane release measured 4.52, 4.09 and 4.19 ms.
2. **A policy pause whose block cleared before `.paused` arrived left the member parked for good (T17, PROBE-C9C-1a/1b).**
   - Fix (4e1de3f): after its await, paused() re-reads laneWideBlock under the current conditions. It parks the job with the block the lane gives now, or re-queues it at the front if the lane is admitted.
   - The f-2 REENTRANCY row is amended.
3. **An offline failure that arrived after the network returned waited for an edge that had already passed (R-SYN-13 [MUST], PROBE-C9C-3).**
   - Fix (5613fe6): EngineState.networkEdgeSerial counts satisfied edges, and ActiveAttempt.edgeSerial records the count when an attempt starts.
   - An `.offline` failure re-queues its job if an edge was applied since the attempt started and the path reads satisfied now. Otherwise it fails whenOnline as before.
   - This allows at most one immediate retry per edge, so it is not polling. A pin test covers the other order (the path dropped again).

**Non-blocking fixes**
- **withdraw no longer scans every job.** It now touches only the waiter's own job (a1e0bc1). A new invariant flags a waiter interest held in any other job. Benchmark: 5.28, 6.25 and 5.67 ms with the old body, 0.017 to 0.021 ms after.
- **Lane-park continuation now has a test.** The new test (b89126c) fails under mutant M-LANEOWED, with 64 members left queued.
- **New cooldown-end benchmark.** Breaker cooldown end over 10,000 parked members (886a2e4): 5.20, 5.28 and 5.39 ms.
- **Further tests (48d09d8).** Unit test of the LaneQueues set-aside, a lane park during a release, and an invariant-oracle test for the two new invariants.
- **Mutants run.** M-LANEOWED, M-ASIDEJOIN and M-ASIDE each fail a cycle-10 test.
- **docs/adr-drafts/f.md.** Records:
  - F-30 with a dispositions table covering every finding.
  - F-14 and F-17 updates.
  - Cycle-10 notes on rulings L4-R1..R15 under "Orchestrator ruling (close-out)". The l4-rulings.md file was re-read and is unchanged.
  - The L4-R12 cycle-9 note corrected to six tests, naming c75a3b9.
  - The merge note now reads F-1…F-30.

All edits are in WP-F files only. No contract signature changed, and Package.swift, Scripts/ and shared docs are untouched. The worktree is clean, the simulator is shut down, and none of my processes are still running.

declined: The space-admitted accounting change was not made (by-reading finding). The sweep's `ahead` already equals what the gate counts in flight for the jobs ahead of it: their ledgerBytes, which is the entry's size. Counting the larger ENOSPC figure there would make the sweep refuse jobs the gate would start. Recorded in F-30.
The verifier's option (c), coalescing the drains' pumps, was not done. Once entries are set aside, each drain's pump scans nothing, so it is not needed.
apply(_:) still does not clear policyPause on in-flight jobs (optional). The pause has already gone to the transport, and paused() now decides on the current verdict for both orders.
The lane park's own set-aside was dropped in 51ef016. The pump's next scan sets the same entries aside, and no test could tell the two apart.

The L4-R4 timed-backoff question, the carried L4-R5/F-28 residue, the outside-wp P-13/P-2/P-5 failures and ZTronAssetKit coverage, and host hygiene (PIDs 27626, 52290, 53148) were left untouched. They are for the orchestrator, as recorded in f.md.
